name: @kitora/display
description: Kitora's data display components: code blocks with a built-in highlighter, description lists, a JSON viewer, timelines, stat cards with sparklines, avatars with presence, person cards, badges, count badges and tags, a copy button, a carousel, a masonry layout that keeps reading order, accordion and tab variants, hints, hover cards and an image gallery on the overlay kit's Lightbox.

The exact lines for `code`, waiting for the engine if it is loading: for a server render or a build step that hands

exports.name: Highlighter
exports.description:
The one highlighting seam of kitora: code and a language in, one token array per line out. Every component that
shows code read-only (display's `CodeBlock` and `CodeTabs`, editors' `HighlightedCode`, the markdown preview, the
rich-text code block, ai-chat's code blocks) asks the highlighter in scope and never an engine, so a host swaps the
engine for all of them with one provider (`DisplayProvider adapters={{ highlighter }}` or `HighlighterProvider`).

`highlight` may answer at once (the built-in regex highlighter) or with a promise (an engine that loads a grammar on
demand, such as `@kitora/display/shiki`). While a promise is pending the component draws `fallback`, then the
exact lines. Both must hold the same text split at the same newlines, so the swap never moves the layout. The text
of a line's tokens, concatenated, is that line of `code` (a trailing newline adds no empty last line).

exports.name: builtinHighlighter
exports.description: The kit's own regex highlighter (core/highlight): no dependency, 16 languages, answers at once.

exports.description:

against: `options.now` (or `null` when there is none) until mounted, then, when live, the wall
clock, re-read every second under a minute away, every minute under an hour, hourly beyond.

exports.name: Highlighter
exports.description:
The one highlighting seam of kitora: code and a language in, one token array per line out. Every component that
shows code read-only (display's `CodeBlock` and `CodeTabs`, editors' `HighlightedCode`, the markdown preview, the
rich-text code block, ai-chat's code blocks) asks the highlighter in scope and never an engine, so a host swaps the
engine for all of them with one provider (`DisplayProvider adapters={{ highlighter }}` or `HighlighterProvider`).

`highlight` may answer at once (the built-in regex highlighter) or with a promise (an engine that loads a grammar on
demand, such as `@kitora/display/shiki`). While a promise is pending the component draws `fallback`, then the
exact lines. Both must hold the same text split at the same newlines, so the swap never moves the layout. The text
of a line's tokens, concatenated, is that line of `code` (a trailing newline adds no empty last line).
